archetype.name: Play-In Team (shooting without stops)
archetype.definition: A veteran-built club whose shot-making should keep it near the middle of the West, but whose turnovers, rebounding and paint defense cap it at fighting for a play-in slot rather than a top-six seed.

report.headline: Elite shooting can't cover the turnovers and an open paint
report.take:
The Clippers are 2-7, fourth in the Pacific, and 21st on the site. The record is mostly earned. A Net Rtg of -4 ranks 20th, the W vs Pt Diff of -1 says they are only about one win short of what the margin implies, and the one coin-flip they lost, a 116-117 overtime loss to Miami, doesn't change the picture. This is a team that has played like a below-average side, not a good team catching bad bounces.

The odd part is that the shooting has been excellent. Their 38.7% from three ranks 2nd, eFG % is 8th and TS % is 7th, all comfortably above the league. Yet the offense ranks only 19th, at a 111.8 ORtg. That gap comes from the possessions that never reach a shot: a 16.7 TOV % that ranks 29th, 2.9 above the league, plus below-average offensive rebounding. Good shooting on too few shots is how you end up scoring less than the league average. The defense is the bigger problem. Opponents are getting to the rim on 34.2% of their shots (26th) and finishing 70.1% there (24th). Both are well past anything in the recent history, and the rebounding (27th in RPG) gives back second chances on top of that.

The roster numbers explain much of it. Darius Garland is taking the most possessions (28.9 USG %) and shooting efficiently enough at 59.9 TS %, but his BPM is -3.2, his On-Off is -37 and he sits 75th of 83 on the point guard tab. Kris Dunn, a low-usage defender, is 7th of 106 among shooting guards with a +14.2 On-Off. Rui Hachimura's 48.9 TS % and -4.9 BPM drag on a frontcourt graded C-. Brook Lopez (66.6 TS %, +10.1 On-Off) is the one big who is clearly working, and Isaiah Jackson, the most active rebounder per minute, is listed Out. Nine-game On-Off figures are noisy, but they all point the same way: the lineups built around ball security and defense have been fine, and the ones built around Garland and Hachimura have not.

History is the reason not to bury them. This franchise went 42-40 last year and 50-32 with a 3rd-ranked defense the year before. The shooting will likely cool off from 2nd in the league, though, so any recovery has to come from cutting turnovers and walling off the paint. Otherwise the 18-win pace shrinks only into the low 30s, not into the playoffs.

strengths.title: Shot-making among the league's best
strengths.body: They hit 38.7% of their threes, 2nd in the league and 4 points above average, which lifts eFG % to 8th. The shot diet is ordinary, so this comes from making shots rather than generating extra attempts. Expect some cooling, but recent Clippers teams have shot 36-38% from three, so a good-shooting team is real even if a top-two one probably isn't.

strengths.title: Dunn and Lopez anchor the good minutes
strengths.body: Kris Dunn ranks 7th of 106 at his position with a 3.5 BPM while using only 12.6% of possessions. Brook Lopez is scoring at a 66.6 TS % with a +10.1 On-Off. These two are doing the low-glamour work the team otherwise lacks, and both profiles, efficient low-usage defense and spacing from the center spot, tend to hold up.

concerns.title: The paint is wide open
concerns.body: Opponents take 34.2% of their shots at the rim, 26th in the league, and make 70.1% of them, 24th. No recent Clippers team allowed rim finishing like that. It is the main reason the 115.8 DRtg ranks 23rd. With Jackson out and Lopez the lone rim protector, this probably doesn't fix itself quickly.

concerns.title: Turnovers waste the good shooting
concerns.body: A 16.7 TOV % ranks 29th and sits 2.9 above the league, well above the 12-13% range of the last five seasons. It is the main reason a top-ten shooting team has a below-average offense. Because it breaks so sharply from history, this is the most fixable problem, but it hasn't improved yet.

concerns.title: Defense sliding, and guards feasting
concerns.body: Over the last five games the Clippers allowed 123.2 a game, 6.76 more than their season average. Opposing shooting guards are piling up more points, rebounds and assists over their own averages than against anyone else in the league. The Garland-led backcourt (C-) is a defensive target, and his -37 On-Off, noisy as it is, fits that picture.

trend.note: October's problem was scoring (105.4 a game). November fixed that at 121.25 but gave up 122.25, so the offense recovered while the defense came apart. The 139-123 win over New Orleans broke a seven-game losing streak without breaking the pattern.

weekAhead.headline: Two winnable games bracket a test against the league's best defense
weekAhead.body:
Phoenix and Charlotte are the kind of opponents a 2-7 team needs. The Suns rank 27th in DRtg and last in defensive rebounding. The Hornets have the league's worst offense at a 101 ORtg and allow opponents 40.8% from three, also the worst. Both games set up for the Clippers' shooting to matter. The road trip to Phoenix is the riskier of the two, because the Suns finish well at the rim on defense (3rd in Opp Rim FG %) and score heavily through their point guards.

Oklahoma City is a different problem. The Thunder's 105.5 DRtg is 1st, they allow the lowest eFG % and rim percentage in the league, and they turn it over only 11.6% of the time, so the Clippers won't get easy points off mistakes. It is also the one place their own turnovers will be punished hardest. Going 2-1 is a realistic and necessary target; anything less keeps them on the current pace.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances at Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: The Suns rank 30th in DRB % and REB %, and opposing centers score 25 a game against them, 29th. That is an opening for Lopez and for a Clippers team that has been below average on the offensive glass. Winning the boards here would hide one of their weaknesses for a night.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security against OKC
keyMatchups.body: Against the league's top defense, which allows only 48.4 Opp eFG %, the Clippers can't afford their 29th-ranked turnover rate. If they reach their shots, their shooting gives them a puncher's chance. If they don't, this game gets away from them.

keyMatchups.title: Threes against Charlotte
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte allows the highest Opp 3P % in the league and gives up 30.1 points a game to point guards. That sets up a volume night for the Clippers' shooters and for Garland in particular. A team this cold on offense should not keep pace with a 38.7% three-point team.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the rim defense tightens without Isaiah Jackson: opponents' shots and makes in the paint will tell you more than the scores.

restOfSeason.body:
The 18-win pace overstates the damage. The margin is closer to a three-win start than a two-win one, the turnover rate is far out of line with this franchise's recent seasons, and the frontcourt should get Jackson back. Expect the turnovers to come down and the record to climb toward the low-to-mid 30s in wins. The three-point shooting is likely to slip back toward its usual 36-37% range, which will offset some of that gain.

The ceiling depends on the defense. Recent Clippers teams with a top-ten defense won 50. Teams in the high teens finished around .500. This one is 23rd and getting worse, with a rim-protection problem the roster may not have the size to fix. Unless the Garland and Hachimura minutes start producing much better results, this projects as a play-in hopeful, not a playoff lock.
swingFactors: Turnover rate returning toward its usual 13%
Rim defense once Isaiah Jackson returns
Whether Garland's minutes stop bleeding points

confidence.note: Nine games; the On-Off and shooting numbers are especially noisy.
